name: rheumatology investigations overview
title: Lab tests for a suspected connective tissue disease: the ANA is the screen and is ordered only when a connective tissue disease is suspected; anti-DNA, the ENA panel and complement follow only a positive ANA; each column gives when to order the test, what a result means, and when not to order it

root.title: Suspected connective tissue disease (CTD): which lab test, and when NOT to order it?
lines: no blood test diagnoses a CTD alone: clinical features are needed too
about 1 in 3 women are ANA positive; lupus (SLE) is 1 in 1,000

head: h
ANA
antibodies against the cell nucleus
when: • sun rash, high creatine kinase, new weakness
• oral ulcers, hair loss, low white cells + platelets
dont: • negative a year ago, no new symptoms
• a past positive still counts for SLE

head: h
Anti-DNA
against DNA in the nucleus
dont: also detect single-stranded DNA: neither sensitive nor specific

head: h
ENA panel
extractable nuclear antigens
means: • Ro: SLE photosensitive rash; baby: heart block
dont: the ENA is a follow-up test

head: h
Complement C3, C4
means: active SLE, esp. lupus nephritis (used up)
